```{python}
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.abspath("."))

import re as _re

DOC = "PCP-007"
UO = "cex"
UO_TITLE = "Cation Exchange Chromatography (Step 7)"

# --- the step and its parameters (config) -------------------------------------------------
uo = CFG.unit_op(UO)
STEP = uo.step
P = {p.key: p for p in uo.parameters}
NM = {k: p.name for k, p in P.items()}                      # as the config names them
nm = {k: _re.sub(r"(^|/)([A-Z])(?=[a-z])", lambda m: m.group(1) + m.group(2).lower(), v)

Nm = {k: v[0].upper() + v[1:] for k, v in nm.items()}       # at the start of a sentence

    # the range studied is wider than the NOR at both ends for every parameter

crit_resp = [r for r in RESP + [FRAG] if D.effective_acceptance(UO, r) is not None]
assert crit_resp == ["aggregate_out_pct", "hcp_out_ng_mg", FRAG]
assert all(D.effective_acceptance(UO, r)[2] == "upper" for r in crit_resp)

assert bool(iac.loc["hcp_out_ng_mg", "widened"]) and not bool(iac.loc["hcp_out_ng_mg", "tightened"])

aexv = D.iac_verification("aex").set_index("cqa").loc["hcp"]

s_agg_v1, s_hcp_v1, s_agg_mg, s_hcp_mg = f"{agg_v1:g}", f"{hcp_v1:.0f}", f"{agg_mg:g}", f"{hcp_mg:g}"

wc_tab = pd.DataFrame([[_attr(c), f"{ver.loc[c, 'assumed']:g}", _upstream(c),

alpha, alpha_lof, gap = THRESHOLDS["effect_alpha"], THRESHOLDS["lof_alpha"], THRESHOLDS["max_r2_minus_pred_r2"]

s_vb = f"{100 * D.VERIFICATION_BOUND:.0f} %"

s_grid, s_mc, s_seed = f"{D.PAR_GRID}", f"{D.PAR_MC_N:,}", f"{D.PAR_SEED}"
```

# Purpose and scope {#sec-purpose}

The A-Mab drug substance process is being transferred from the development site in `{python} SENDING_LOCATION`, to the commercial drug substance site in `{python} RECEIVING_LOCATION`, under the Process Transfer Plan PTP-001. This plan describes the Stage 1 characterization of cation exchange chromatography, which is Step `{python} STEP` of the drug substance train and its principal polishing step [@fda2011]. The studies are run on a qualified scale-down model of the commercial column. At the receiving site the process runs at a production bioreactor scale of `{python} f"{V['commercial_scale_l']:,}"` L.

The studies measure how far the aggregate, host cell protein and fragment content of the eluate pool, and the step yield, move as each parameter is varied across its range studied (@tbl-params). The results define the region in which the pool meets its criteria, and they justify the ranges and controls applied in commercial manufacture.

The plan covers the `{python} n_par` process parameters of the step. The risk assessment RA-001 assigned `{python} n_mv` of them to a multivariate design and `{python} nm["flow"]` to a univariate assessment. The plan also covers the size variants and process impurities that the step clears, and the step yield. The step is fed with the neutralized pool of low-pH viral inactivation. The attributes of that pool are inputs to the study, not factors of it.

Three activities lie outside this plan. Resin life cycle, sanitization and repacking are qualified under the resin life cycle procedure SOP-2008, and the studies use resin within its qualified life. The analytical methods are validated under the method validations listed in @tbl-sops, and this plan uses them as validated. Confirmation of the ranges at commercial scale belongs to Stage 2 and to the process performance qualification (PPQ) batches that follow the transfer.

No viral clearance claim is made for cation exchange. Clearance of enveloped virus is claimed at low-pH viral inactivation, anion exchange and virus filtration, and clearance of parvovirus at anion exchange and virus filtration. The master report PCMR-001 consolidates the cumulative claim [@ichq5a]. Cation exchange contributes clearance of host cell protein, residual DNA and leached Protein A, and these contributions are in scope.

## Changes in this revision {#sec-changes}

Version 1.0 of this plan was approved on `{python} v1_date`, before the first study of the step started on `{python} first_start`. The studies it governs ran until `{python} last_end` (@sec-schedule). Version 2.0, effective `{python} v2_date`, is issued after them under the Quality Assurance (QA) investigation INV-001 (`{python} INV["title"]`). QA opened the investigation on `{python} INV["opened"]`, after reviewing the master report PCMR-001 Version 1.0 for the Biologics License Application (BLA). It closed the investigation on `{python} INV["closed"]` with the classification `{python} INV["classification"]`. INV-001 found that the criteria used to judge each step in the proven acceptable range (PAR) analysis had been set after the data were seen and were in no approved protocol (INV-001 finding 1).

The revision is issued under INV-002 as well (`{python} INV2["title"]`). That investigation applied the model adequacy criteria of the master plan PCMP-001 §7.2, which this plan states in @sec-adequacy, to every response-surface model of the campaign whose output has a criterion. The report PCR-007 gives its outcome for this step.

This revision keeps the design and the sampling of Version 1.0, and every decision rule of Version 1.0 that PCMP-001 Version 2.0 does not replace. Where a study departed from them, PCR-007 records the departure. Each change below applies a rule of PCMP-001 Version 2.0 to this step, and names the Version 1.0 rule it replaces.

1. Intermediate acceptance criteria replace the Version 1.0 limits. Version 1.0 judged the pool against an aggregate limit of `{python} s_agg_v1` % high molecular weight species (HMW) and a host cell protein limit of `{python} s_hcp_v1` ng/mg. Each limit was the drug substance criterion carried back through the nominal clearance of the later steps in this campaign and then divided by a margin, `{python} s_agg_mg` for aggregate and `{python} s_hcp_mg` for host cell protein (INV-001 finding 2). Version 2.0 judges the pool against the intermediate acceptance criteria of PCMP-001 §7.3, which are derived a priori from the drug substance criteria and the platform worst cases of the downstream steps (@sec-iac). @tbl-criteria-change compares the two versions. The Version 2.0 criteria for aggregate and host cell protein are wider than the Version 1.0 limits. The Version 1.0 limits were applied at analysis and were in no approved plan (INV-001 finding 1).
2. Fragments are judged at this step, by one method. Version 1.0 did not assess fragments here. Version 2.0 judges them against the drug substance criterion of `{python} s_frag` % and measures them by non-reduced capillary electrophoresis with sodium dodecyl sulfate (nrCE-SDS). From `{python} AMD["date"]` this is the method for fragments in every study at every step, following the analytical method decision `{python} AMD["id"]` (PCMP-001 §7.8). The decision answers INV-001 finding 6, that size exclusion chromatography (SEC) reads fragments high in samples that still carry host cell protein. That finding came from a comparability study on samples of this step and of the steps around it (@sec-methods).
3. The scale-down model is qualified by its offset. Version 1.0 accepted the model before any characterization run, where no statistically significant difference was found between the scales. Version 2.0 qualifies the model for each output by its offset from manufacturing scale and states every judgement against a criterion at manufacturing scale. The qualification runs and the offset estimates still come before the first characterization run. The decision whether the model is qualified for an output is made at analysis (@sec-sdm and @sec-qualification).
4. Model adequacy is judged by four tests. Version 1.0 judged a model on its F-test and its lack of fit, and asked only that R², adjusted R² and predicted R² lie close to one another. Version 2.0 applies the four tests of PCMP-001 §7.2. They include a limit on the difference between R² and predicted R², and this plan states the tests on the residuals and on influence with their cut-offs (@sec-adequacy).
5. Each output is judged on a single batch. The NOR-propagated analysis scans one parameter across its range studied while the other parameters are drawn from distributions centred on their set-points that span their normal operating ranges (NORs). Version 1.0 accepted a setting in that analysis where the predicted values met the criterion across the draws, and it did not define the distribution of the draws. Version 2.0 judges each output with a criterion on a single batch, through a `{python} s_pi` prediction interval, and defines the distribution (@sec-judgement and @sec-par).
6. The platform worst cases of this step are verified. PCR-007 checks the platform worst cases of cation exchange on which the criteria upstream rely, and the rule of PCMP-001 §7.5 decides whether a check changes a criterion (@sec-verification). Version 1.0 had no such check, because it had no criteria derived from platform worst cases.
7. Each class is argued from two stated values. Version 1.0 named the two grounds of a class, the size of the effect and the risk that the parameter leaves the operating region, but not the values on which the report states them. PCR-007 states for each parameter the size of its effect across its PAR and the margin of the PAR to the NOR, and it gives the reason for each class on these two values (@sec-classification). Neither PCMP-001 nor the parameter classification procedure SOP-4001 sets a numerical threshold for an effect that matters or a range that is wide.
8. Capability thresholds are set for the drug substance. As in Version 1.0, no minimum capability index is set for the outputs of this step. PCMP-001 Version 2.0 sets the campaign thresholds against which PCMR-001 judges the capability of the drug substance (@sec-stats).
9. The execution record is complete. The Version 1.0 records gave no execution dates, and the title block of Version 1.0 carried `{python} rev1_eff`, the date on which the Version 1.0 reports were approved (INV-001 finding 5). This revision records the approval date of Version 1.0, the execution window of each study and the calibration status of the equipment it used (@sec-schedule).

```{python}
T.criteria_change([UO]).show()
```

Applying the criteria of this revision to studies already executed is acceptable because their derivation uses no result of those studies (PCMP-001 §7.3). The drug substance criteria come from the register of critical quality attributes (CQAs), and the worst cases come from the platform history of X-Mab, Y-Mab and Z-Mab. The one A-Mab value in a criterion of this step is a result of the anion exchange step downstream (@sec-iac).

# Objectives {#sec-objectives}

The study has six objectives.

1. To quantify the relationship between each studied parameter and each response of the step, over ranges wider than those in which the step will be operated.
2. To define the multivariate region over which the fitted models predict that every output with a criterion at this step meets its intermediate acceptance criterion at manufacturing scale (@tbl-iac).
3. To establish a PAR for each parameter of the designs against each output with a criterion, both with the other parameters at their set-points and with the other parameters drawn from distributions centred on their set-points that span their NORs (@sec-par).
4. To verify the platform worst cases of cation exchange on which the criteria upstream rely (@sec-verification).
5. To classify each parameter under the parameter classification procedure SOP-4001, from the size of its demonstrated effect and from the capability with which the parameter is controlled.
6. To state the ranges, in-process controls and monitoring that this step contributes to the control strategy, and to justify them for Stage 2.

The report PCR-007 presents the outcome against each of these objectives.

# Prior knowledge and quality risk basis {#sec-prior}

## Unit-operation description and prior knowledge {#sec-uo}

Cation exchange is operated in bind and elute mode and is the principal aggregate polishing step of the purification train. Below its isoelectric point the antibody carries a net positive charge and binds the negatively charged ligand of the resin. Raising the pH of the elution buffer weakens this electrostatic attraction and elutes the antibody. Aggregate presents more positive charge to the ligand than monomer does, because a dimer carries twice the charged surface. Aggregate is therefore retained more strongly and elutes after the monomer. The clearance of aggregate depends on how well the two peaks are resolved and on where collection of the pool stops.

The process impurities leave the column during the load and the wash. Most host cell proteins are acidic at the operating pH and do not bind the resin, so they leave in the load flow-through. The weakly bound remainder is displaced in the wash. DNA is strongly negatively charged and is repelled by the ligand, so it passes through in the load. Its clearance is large and is not expected to depend on the operating parameters. Leached Protein A and its fragments are acidic and do not bind under load conditions. The part that is complexed with the antibody is released when the antibody binds the ligand, and it passes through as well. The step clears leached Protein A by a modest factor that is a property of the chemistry and not of any parameter studied here.

Fragments carry less positive charge than intact antibody at the binding pH and elute on the leading side of the main peak, so the leading fractions are rich in fragments. The points at which collection starts and stops change the share of fragments in the pool. The step is expected to clear part of the fragment load, not all of it. Yield is lost at the two edges of the pool. Monomer that elutes after the stop collect point stays in the tail, and monomer that elutes with the aggregate that is cut away is lost with it.

The step has been run on the Novacyte humanized immunoglobulin G1 (IgG1) platform for three earlier products, X-Mab, Y-Mab and Z-Mab, and throughout A-Mab clinical and engineering manufacture [@amab2009]. The resin chemistry, the buffer system and the mode of operation are unchanged for A-Mab. This experience establishes the mechanisms above and identifies the parameters worth studying. The studies are therefore designed to confirm and bound platform behaviour, not to discover it. Prior knowledge enters the plan in two further ways. It gives the expected direction of each effect, listed below. It also supplies the platform worst cases of the downstream steps, from which the criteria of this step are derived (@sec-iac), and the platform worst cases of this step, on which the criteria upstream rely (@sec-verification). Every range reported in PCR-007 rests on data from the studies of this plan.

The platform experience gives four expectations, and the multivariate design is built to test them.

- `{python} Nm["load"]` sets how much of the ligand is occupied. As the load approaches the dynamic binding capacity, the monomer and aggregate peaks broaden and overlap more, and weakly bound host cell protein finds fewer free sites from which the wash would displace it. Aggregate clearance, host cell protein clearance and yield are therefore expected to fall together as the load rises.
- `{python} Nm["wash_cond"]` sets the ionic strength that shields the charges on the ligand and on the bound species. A higher conductivity is expected to strip more weakly bound host cell protein during the wash, while the antibody, which binds more strongly, stays on the column. Its effect is expected on impurity clearance and not on the aggregate separation, which takes place during elution.
- `{python} Nm["elution_ph"]` sets the net charge of the antibody at the moment of elution. A higher pH within the range weakens binding and brings monomer and aggregate off earlier and closer together. It is expected to reduce the resolution on which aggregate clearance depends.
- `{python} Nm["stop_collect"]` decides how much of the descending edge of the peak enters the pool. Aggregate elutes on that edge, so a later stop is expected to recover more monomer and to take in the front of the aggregate peak, and an earlier stop the reverse. It is the direct handle on the balance between aggregate and yield.

`{python} Nm["flow"]` sets the residence time during elution and with it the sharpness of the peaks. Over the range studied, and at the particle size of the platform resin, the change in sharpness is expected to be too small to move the aggregate content of the pool. For this reason it is assessed one factor at a time (@sec-risk).

## Quality attributes in scope {#sec-cqa}

Cation exchange forms no quality attribute of its own. Aggregate is formed in the production bioreactor and increases during the low-pH hold. Host cell protein and residual DNA enter with the harvested cell culture fluid, leached Protein A is released from the capture resin, and fragments are formed in culture and during the harvest hold. This step removes part of each. @tbl-cqa lists the attributes in scope with their drug substance criteria and their criticality. Criticality was assigned with Tool #1 of the A-Mab case study, as the product of impact and uncertainty, on a continuum from very low (VL) to very high (VH) [@amab2009; @ichq9]. Attributes of high (H) and very high criticality are called critical.

```{python}
#| output: asis
T.frame(cq_tab, cap_cq, "tbl-cqa", merge=["Category"], align=["P{2.6cm}", "P{4.6cm}", "P{3.4cm}", "l", "r"], notes=cq_note).show()
```

Aggregate is the attribute the step exists to control, and no step after cation exchange changes it in the derivation of the criteria (@sec-iac). Host cell protein is cleared here and again at anion exchange, so this step must hand on a pool that anion exchange can bring to the drug substance criterion. Fragments are a response of the response-surface design, measured by nrCE-SDS (@sec-methods), and are judged against the drug substance criterion.

Residual DNA and leached Protein A are measured across the step so that their clearance is confirmed. Neither is a response of the designs. DNA is repelled by the ligand at every conductivity and pH in @tbl-params, and leached Protein A stays unbound over the same range. PCR-007 reports the clearance of both and claims a dependence on a parameter for neither unless the data show one.

Step yield is a measure of process performance, not a quality attribute. It is measured on every run because the monomer cut away with the aggregate is lost from the pool, so the aggregate clearance and the yield of a setting have to be read together. It has no acceptance criterion.

## Risk-based prioritization of parameters {#sec-risk}

The risk assessment RA-001 set the scope of this study. Every process parameter of the step was ranked for its potential impact on a quality attribute and, separately, for its potential to interact with other parameters. The two rankings were combined into a study assignment [@amab2009]. Where no data or rationale were available, a parameter was ranked at the highest level.

The assignment gave three groups. The multivariate design carries `{python} n_mv` parameters. `{python} Nm["load"]`, `{python} nm["elution_ph"]` and `{python} nm["stop_collect"]` each move the aggregate peak relative to the point at which collection stops. `{python} Nm["load"]` also acts with `{python} nm["wash_cond"]` to set how much weakly bound host cell protein survives the wash. For this reason their effects on the pool cannot be assumed to add. `{python} Nm["flow"]` was assigned to a univariate assessment, because it changes the residence time of the antibody in the pores of the resin and not the strength with which the antibody binds the ligand. Its expected effect on the separation is small. Parameters fixed by equipment design or held to platform specification, such as bed height, column packing quality and buffer composition, were not assigned a new study. Their ranges rest on the platform knowledge space and on the operation and life cycle procedures in @tbl-sops.

The range studied of every parameter is wider than its NOR at both ends (@tbl-params). Each range was set from the control capability of the commercial equipment and from the range over which the platform has been operated. The study therefore bounds the step beyond the region in which it will run, and it supports later movement within the region it defines [@ichq8]. Ranges were not widened past the point at which the step would fail for a reason already understood. The range of `{python} nm["elution_ph"]` stops short of the pH at which the antibody would no longer bind reproducibly. A run at such a pH would confirm the mechanism and would say nothing about the operating region.

# Materials and methods {#sec-mm}

## Scale-down model and its qualification {#sec-sdm}

The studies are run on a laboratory column packed with the same resin and to the same bed height as the commercial column, and operated at the same linear velocities. Protein load is set in grams of antibody per litre of resin, and the equilibration, wash, elution and strip volumes in column volumes. In this way every parameter of the study is expressed at its commercial equivalent. Packing quality is verified before each campaign by plate count and peak asymmetry, and a column that fails either test is repacked before use. The scale-down model procedure SOP-1001 and the operating procedure SOP-2010 describe the model and its operation.

The qualification runs come first. Before the first characterization run of the step, the model is run at the set-point of every parameter in @tbl-params and its outputs are compared with manufacturing-scale batches (SOP-1001). The comparison covers the attributes that enter and leave the step, which are step yield, pool aggregate, pool host cell protein, residual DNA and leached Protein A. Plate count and peak asymmetry, which describe the efficiency of the column, are compared as well (PCMP-001 §5). The qualification uses `{python} n_sdm` scale-down runs at set-point and `{python} n_mfg` A-Mab batches at manufacturing scale.

The offset of each output is estimated from these runs, also before the first characterization run. The offset is the mean of the scale-down runs minus the mean of the manufacturing-scale batches, with its two-sided `{python} s_offci` confidence interval. Each end of that interval is a one-sided `{python} s_side` confidence bound. Whether the model is qualified for an output is decided later, at analysis. The decision compares the conclusion over the NOR with the offset at either end of its interval, and that conclusion comes from the response-surface model (@sec-qualification).

Pool aggregate and pool host cell protein are compared at both scales and have a criterion at this step. Every judgement of them against their criterion first subtracts the offset, so their ranges and conclusions are stated at manufacturing scale. Outputs with no criterion at this step have their offsets recorded, and no conclusion depends on them (PCMP-001 §7.1).

The qualification does not compare fragments at both scales. Their offset is therefore unknown, not zero. Fragments are judged as the model predicts them, and no offset is subtracted. That judgement rests on an assumption about the mechanism. The fragment content of the pool depends on the shape of the elution peak and on the absorbance at which collection starts and stops. The scale-down model keeps the bed height, the linear velocity and the absorbance thresholds of the commercial column, and the qualification compares plate count and peak asymmetry, which describe the shape of the peak. Fragments are therefore expected to separate in the same way at both scales.

The centre points of both designs are run at the set-point of every factor. Their spread measures the reproducibility of the model under study conditions and gives the pure error against which lack of fit is tested (@sec-stats).

The claims of this study are bounded by the model. A scale-down column reproduces the chromatography of the commercial column. It does not reproduce the hold times, the pool volumes or the mixing of the commercial suite. Conclusions drawn here apply to the commercial step through the qualification above, and they are confirmed at scale in Stage 2.

## Operation {#sec-operation}

The step is loaded with the neutralized pool of low-pH viral inactivation. The pool is adjusted to the load conductivity under study and loaded onto the equilibrated column at the protein load under study. The column is then washed at the same conductivity as the load. One buffer therefore sets the ionic strength of both operations, and the two cannot be varied independently. Elution is a step change to the elution buffer at the pH under study, at the elution flow rate set for the run. The pool is collected from a threshold on the ascending edge of the elution peak to the stop collect threshold on the descending edge, both read as ultraviolet absorbance (OD280). After collection the column is stripped, sanitized and re-equilibrated under the resin life cycle procedure SOP-2008.

Buffer preparation, column packing and resin storage are held to platform specification under the procedures in @tbl-sops. They are controlled inputs to the study, not factors of it. Temperature is held constant and is not varied, because the platform runs the step at controlled room temperature at both sites and the transfer introduces no difference in that control. A parameter that a run does not vary is held at its set-point (@tbl-params).

## Analytical methods {#sec-methods}

Each response and each attribute in scope is measured by a validated method (@tbl-sops). Pool aggregate is measured by size exclusion chromatography (SEC, AMV-3011) and reported as the percentage of high molecular weight species. Host cell protein is measured by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA, AMV-3012) and reported per milligram of antibody, so that the result does not move with the concentration of the pool. Residual DNA is measured by quantitative polymerase chain reaction (qPCR, AMV-3014), and leached Protein A by ELISA (AMV-3016). Step yield is calculated from the antibody mass in the pool and in the load, each determined by ultraviolet absorbance against the extinction coefficient of A-Mab.

Fragments are measured by nrCE-SDS (AMV-3020). From `{python} AMD["date"]`, nrCE-SDS is the method for fragments in every study at every step, following the analytical method decision `{python} AMD["id"]` (PCMP-001 §7.8). One method across the train is needed because fragment results are compared between steps, and a comparison across two methods would mix method bias with step performance. The decision followed the comparability study S-CEX-FRC (`{python} frc["start"]` to `{python} frc["end"]`), in which SEC and nrCE-SDS were run on the same samples, among them samples of this step. SEC read fragments high wherever the sample still carried host cell protein, because part of the host cell protein elutes in the low molecular weight window of SEC and is counted as fragment. The excess can never exceed the host cell protein present. From the cation exchange pool onward the two methods agreed (INV-001 finding 6). SEC remains the method for aggregate, where no such interference applies.

@tbl-methods-by-study shows which method measured fragments in each design of this step. The screening design ran before the decision and measured fragments by SEC. Its samples were not retained and could not be retested by nrCE-SDS. These SEC results are therefore kept in the record and are not used for any decision. The response-surface design ran across the decision date and has results by both methods on the same samples. Fragments are judged on the nrCE-SDS results only.

```{python}
#| output: asis
T.methods_by_study([UO]).show()
```

Assay variability enters the analysis at two points. It is part of the residual variance of each fitted model, and it is part of the centre point spread that estimates pure error. Consequently, a response measured by a less precise assay has a wider prediction interval and a less sensitive test for lack of fit. Where a predicted value lies within assay variability of its criterion, PCR-007 should attribute the result to the assay and should not claim an effect. Host cell protein is expected to be the least reproducible of the responses, and the centre points will show whether that expectation holds.

## Sampling plan {#sec-sampling}

Each run is sampled at four points.

1. The load is sampled after conditioning, so that the aggregate, host cell protein, residual DNA and leached Protein A entering the step are known for every run.
2. The flow-through and the wash are each sampled as a single pooled fraction, so that the host cell protein mass balance across the step can be closed.
3. The eluate pool is sampled after collection and mixing are complete. It carries every response of the study.
4. A strip fraction is sampled and retained. It is tested only where a run fails to close its mass balance.

Replication is concentrated at the centre point. The screening design carries `{python} cp_scr` centre points and the response-surface design `{python} cp_rsm`, each run at the set-point of every factor. Samples are assigned to analytical runs in an order that does not follow the design order, so that drift in an assay cannot align with a factor. Retained samples are held under the conditions and for the period stated in the operating procedure SOP-2010, so that a result can be retested where it is questioned.

## Statistical methods {#sec-stats}

All factors are analysed in coded units. Each factor is coded so that the centre of its range studied is 0 and its ends are −1 and +1. At this step the centre of each range is the set-point (@tbl-params). Coding makes the estimated effects comparable across factors with different units, and it makes the intercept the predicted response at the set-point. The letter codes of @tbl-factors are used for the terms of both models.

The screening design is analysed by ordinary least squares with all main effects and all two-factor interactions. An effect is reported as twice the coded coefficient, which is the change in the response across the full range studied of that factor. A term is significant when its p-value is below α = `{python} alpha`, the level that PCMP-001 §6.2 sets for model terms. The screening analysis identifies which factors and which interactions change each response, and by how much. It is not the predictive model of the step. Its centre points detect curvature but cannot attribute it to a factor, and a model without quadratic terms interpolates linearly between the corners of the design. The response-surface model is the predictive model. The operating region, the PARs, the judgement over the NOR, the verification of the platform worst cases and the capability estimate all come from it.

The response-surface design is analysed with a full quadratic model in the `{python} k` factors, with main effects, two-factor interactions and pure quadratic terms. With the intercept the model has `{python} n_terms` terms. Each fitted model is reported with R², adjusted R² and predicted R², the last computed from the prediction error sum of squares (PRESS). It is also reported with the model F-test and with the test for lack of fit against the pure error from the centre points. The residuals are plotted against the predicted values and against the run order, and on a normal probability plot. The influence of each run is given by its Cook's distance. @sec-adequacy states the tests a model must pass before it is used for prediction.

A factor with no significant term in either model is reported as having no demonstrated effect on that response. That statement is bounded by the range studied and by the power of the design. PCR-007 states it in those terms, not as an absence of effect in general.

A prediction interval for a single run is exact. It uses the t distribution and includes both the residual variance and the uncertainty of the fitted coefficients. For pool aggregate and pool host cell protein it is computed at manufacturing scale, by subtracting the offset of @sec-sdm.

Capability is estimated by Monte Carlo simulation. The simulation draws `{python} s_nmc` batches. Each parameter is drawn from the same normal distribution as in the NOR-propagated analysis of @sec-par, the fitted models are evaluated at each draw, and a one-sided process capability index (Cpk) is computed for each output with a criterion in @tbl-iac. This plan sets no minimum capability index for the outputs of this step. The decision rules are those of @sec-criteria. The capability estimate is reported beside them as supporting evidence, with the margin between the predicted distribution and the criterion. The capability of the drug substance is estimated from the integrated model of the train. PCMR-001 judges it against the campaign thresholds of PCMP-001 §7.9, a target Cpk of `{python} s_cpk_t` and a minimum of `{python} s_cpk_m`.

Both analyses of the PAR determination (@sec-par) use the response-surface model, and its Monte Carlo part uses a fixed random seed, so that a repeat of the analysis on the recorded data returns the same ranges.

The table carries no classification, because classification is an outcome of the study, reported in PCR-007 under the parameter classification procedure SOP-4001.

## Screening design {#sec-screening}

The screening study is a two-level full factorial design in the `{python} k` multivariate factors, with `{python} n_fact_scr` factorial runs and `{python} cp_scr` centre points, `{python} n_scr` runs in total. A full factorial was chosen over a fraction for two reasons. The number of factors is small, and `{python} nm["load"]` is expected to interact with each of the other factors through the peak broadening that rising ligand occupancy produces. A resolution IV fraction would alias these two-factor interactions with each other in pairs, and the analysis could not say which of them is active. The full factorial estimates every main effect and every two-factor interaction independently.

The runs are made in random order. The centre points are spread through the campaign and not grouped, so that drift in the model or in the feed material shows in the centre point spread and not in a factor effect. All runs are made on a single conditioned feed lot where the available material allows. Where more than one lot is needed, the lot is recorded with the run and the centre points are balanced across lots. Appendix A gives the planned coded design.

## Response-surface design {#sec-rsm}

The response-surface study is a face-centred central composite design in the `{python} k` factors of the screening study. It has `{python} n_fact_rsm` factorial runs, `{python} n_ax` axial runs and `{python} cp_rsm` centre points, `{python} n_rsm` runs in total. The axial runs sit on the faces of the cube, so that no run is made outside the range studied of any factor. The ranges studied are already wider than the NORs, and a rotatable design would need settings outside them for which the step has no prior support.

The design adds the quadratic terms that the screening design cannot estimate. Curvature is expected for `{python} nm["stop_collect"]` and `{python} nm["elution_ph"]`. Both change where the pool is cut relative to the aggregate peak. Because that peak has a maximum, equal steps in the cut point add unequal amounts of aggregate to the pool. Appendix B gives the planned coded design.

The two designs are made in sequence and analysed separately. Should the screening analysis identify an active factor that is not carried into the response-surface design, the design should be augmented before the operating region is declared. The augmentation should then be documented as a change to this plan under @sec-approvals.

## Univariate assessment {#sec-univariate}

`{python} Nm["flow"]` is assessed one factor at a time. Runs are made at the low end, the set-point and the high end of its range studied (@tbl-params), with every other parameter at its set-point. Pool aggregate, pool host cell protein and step yield are measured on each run. The assessment establishes whether a longer residence time sharpens the elution peak enough to change the aggregate content or the yield of the pool over the range studied. It also supports the range within which the flow rate is controlled in manufacture.

A univariate assessment cannot determine whether the flow rate interacts with the other parameters. That limitation is accepted here for a physical reason. The flow rate changes the residence time of the antibody in the pores of the resin, and with it the sharpness of the elution peak. It changes neither the net charge of the antibody nor the ionic strength that sets how strongly the antibody is held. An interaction with `{python} nm["load"]`, `{python} nm["wash_cond"]`, `{python} nm["elution_ph"]` or the collection window is therefore not expected. Should the assessment show an effect on any response comparable in size with the effects estimated in the screening study, the flow rate should be carried into a multivariate study before the operating region is declared.

# Acceptance and decision criteria {#sec-criteria}

The criteria in this section decide whether the scale-down model is qualified for an output, whether a model is adequate, whether an output meets its criterion, where the operating region lies, whether a platform worst case holds and how each parameter is classified. The proven acceptable ranges follow in @sec-par.

## Qualification of the scale-down model {#sec-qualification}

The scale-down model is qualified for each output separately, by its offset from manufacturing scale and not by a test of equivalence (PCMP-001 §7.1). Pool aggregate and pool host cell protein are compared at both scales and have a criterion at this step. For each of them the model is qualified when the conclusion against the criterion over the NOR is the same with the offset at either end of its `{python} s_offci` confidence interval. The conclusion is whether the output meets its criterion at every combination of NOR low, set-point and NOR high of the `{python} k` factors (@sec-judgement). A model whose conclusion changes between the two ends of the interval is not used for that output. Where the cause of an offset is known, PCR-007 states it. Where the model is not qualified for an output, PCR-007 says so and states the consequence.

## Model adequacy {#sec-adequacy}

A response-surface model is used for prediction only if it passes the four tests of PCMP-001 §7.2.

1. The model F-test is significant at α = `{python} alpha`, the level set for model terms.
2. Lack of fit against the pure error from the centre points is not significant at α = `{python} alpha_lof`.
3. Predicted R² falls short of R² by no more than `{python} f"{gap:.2f}"`. This limits overfitting, because a model that fits its own runs much better than it predicts runs left out of the fit has more terms than the data support.
4. The residuals show no pattern against the predicted values or the run order, and no single run dominates the fit. The residuals are regressed on the predicted values and on the run order, and neither slope may be significant at α = `{python} alpha`. No run may have a Cook's distance above 4/n, where n is the number of runs in the fit. Cook's distance measures how far all fitted values move when one run is left out of the fit. The cut-off 4/n is the conventional one, and it falls as the design grows.

The level α = `{python} alpha` is the conventional level for a statistical test. The same level applies to model terms, to lack of fit and to the regressions of the residuals.

A model that fails the test for lack of fit or the limit on overfitting is either refitted with a justified change of terms or transformation, or it is not used to set a range (PCMP-001 §7.2). Where lack of fit is significant, PCR-007 should state whether the cause is a missing term or an outlying run. It should establish that from the residuals and not from the summary statistics alone. Where no adequate model results, PCR-007 reports the output descriptively, against its criterion, over the runs of the designs. Such an output sets no operating region and no PAR. It meets its criterion only if every measured result of the designs meets it at manufacturing scale. For fragments the measured results are the nrCE-SDS results.

## Intermediate acceptance criteria {#sec-iac}

Each output of this step with a criterion is judged against an intermediate acceptance criterion (IAC, @tbl-iac). PCMP-001 §7.3 derives it by carrying the drug substance criterion backward through the train, step by step, with the worst case that each downstream step showed on the platform, X-Mab, Y-Mab and Z-Mab. For a step that removes an attribute the worst case is the lowest clearance fold, and for a step that adds to an attribute it is the largest increase. No margin is applied.

No step after cation exchange changes aggregate or fragments in this derivation. The cation exchange pool therefore carries the drug substance criteria themselves, `{python} s_agg` % for aggregate and `{python} s_frag` % for fragments. For host cell protein the drug substance criterion of `{python} s_ds_hcp` ng/mg is carried back through anion exchange. With the platform worst case of anion exchange, a `{python} s_aex_pf`-fold clearance, the criterion is `{python} s_hcp_ap` ng/mg a priori. The anion exchange report PCR-008 verified that worst case and found a one-sided `{python} s_vb` prediction bound of a single batch of `{python} s_aex_b`-fold, better than the platform value, on a model that meets the adequacy criteria of PCMP-001 §7.2. The bound replaced the platform value, and the criterion in force is `{python} s_hcp` ng/mg.

```{python}
#| output: asis
T.iac_derivation([UO]).show()
```

No result of the studies under this plan enters these criteria. The one A-Mab value in them is the anion exchange bound. Because PCR-007 relies on the widened host cell protein criterion, it gives the bound, the runs behind it and the reason why the performance of anion exchange for A-Mab is known well enough to replace the platform value, and it argues the change by its risk (@sec-verification).

Residual DNA, leached Protein A and step yield have no criterion at this step. The platform history gives no worst-case DNA clearance for the steps after Protein A, so no DNA criterion can be carried back, and residual DNA is judged on the drug substance only. Leached Protein A is judged in the Protein A pool, against a criterion carried back through the platform worst cases of cation exchange and anion exchange. PCR-007 reports the clearance of both, and no range is derived from them.

## Judgement of an output against its criterion {#sec-judgement}

Every output with a criterion at this step is a quality attribute. Its criterion applies to each batch, so each output is judged on a single batch. A response-surface model predicts the mean response, and a single batch scatters around that mean. For this reason the judgement uses a prediction interval or bound of a single batch, which adds the scatter of a batch and the uncertainty of the fitted coefficients to the predicted mean. Three analyses judge an output in this way. They are the judgement over the NOR, which the qualification uses (@sec-qualification), the NOR-propagated PAR (@sec-par) and the verification of the platform worst cases (@sec-verification).

The judgement over the NOR asks whether the exact `{python} s_pi` prediction interval of a single run, at manufacturing scale, lies within the criterion at every one of the `{python} n_comb` combinations of NOR low, set-point and NOR high of the `{python} k` factors. All criteria at this step are upper limits, so the upper end of the interval decides.

No viral clearance claim is made for this step. The rule that PCMP-001 §6.4 sets for viral clearance, the mean predicted log reduction at the least favourable combination of the other parameters, does not apply here.

## Operating region {#sec-region}

The operating region is declared where the fitted models predict, at manufacturing scale, that every output with a criterion in @tbl-iac meets it, over the ranges studied of the `{python} k` factors. The declared region lies inside the ranges studied, and the NORs lie inside the declared region. PCR-007 states the margin between the two and identifies the output and the parameter that bound the region most tightly. Where the models predict that a criterion is met across the whole range studied of a parameter, PCR-007 reports that as the finding. The range is not narrowed to create a margin that the data do not require.

The region is defined on mean predictions. At its edge a single batch meets its criterion only about half the time if variability is symmetrical. For this reason the range that supports a claim is the NOR-propagated PAR of @sec-par.

Step yield has no criterion and does not bound the operating region. PCR-007 reports it across the region as a measure of process performance. A setting that meets every criterion at a cost in yield is described as such and is not excluded.

## Verification of the platform worst cases {#sec-verification}

The criteria upstream of this step assume that cation exchange clears each attribute at least as well as its platform worst case, the lowest clearance fold seen for X-Mab, Y-Mab and Z-Mab. @tbl-worst-cases lists the `{python} n_ver` worst cases of this step and the criteria that rely on each. PCR-007 checks the `{python} n_ver_checked` that are responses of the designs (PCMP-001 §7.5). Leached Protein A is not a response of the designs, so its platform value stands.

```{python}
#| output: asis
T.frame(wc_tab, cap_wc, "tbl-worst-cases", align=["P{3.4cm}", "r", "P{4.0cm}", "P{4.6cm}"]).show()
```

The check evaluates the response-surface model of this step at every combination of NOR low, set-point and NOR high of its `{python} k` factors, the values the studies were planned against. The model gives the lowest clearance fold it predicts over these combinations. It also gives the one-sided `{python} s_vb` prediction bound of a single batch at the least favourable combination. An assumption is confirmed when the predicted worst case is no worse than the platform worst case. The values observed at the ends of the ranges studied are reported beside it for information. A check may change the criteria upstream by the following rule.

1. Where the predicted worst case is worse than the platform worst case, the prediction bound of a single batch replaces the platform value. Every criterion upstream for that attribute is recalculated with it and becomes stricter.
2. Where the prediction bound of a single batch is better than the platform value, and the model behind it passes the tests of @sec-adequacy, the bound replaces the platform value. Every criterion upstream for that attribute is recalculated with it and becomes wider.
3. Otherwise the platform value stands.

In both directions the bound replaces the platform value, and the point prediction never does. The bound is never a confidence bound of the mean. Each worst case concerns a quality attribute, which is judged on a single batch, and the platform value it may replace was itself the result of a single run.

A report whose check changes a criterion argues the change by its risk (PCMP-001 §7.5). It states who bears the risk, the patient or the producer. It states whether an excursion of the step output beyond the changed criterion would be detected, and where, by an in-process test or by a release test. It states what the downstream steps must then clear, and it gives the probability that the drug substance fails its specification in the integrated model of the train.

## Parameter classification {#sec-classification}

Parameters are classified under the parameter classification procedure SOP-4001 by the decision logic of the A-Mab case study [@amab2009] and of PCMP-001 §7.7. A parameter is classified from two things together. The first is the size of the effect the study demonstrates on a quality attribute. The second is the risk that the parameter moves outside the declared region in manufacture.

1. A parameter linked to a quality attribute and held well inside the region by the commercial control system is a well-controlled critical process parameter (WC-CPP).
2. A parameter linked to a quality attribute whose control is narrow against the region is a critical process parameter (CPP).
3. A parameter that changes step yield or another measure of process performance without changing a quality attribute is a key process parameter (KPP).
4. A parameter that changes neither over the range studied is a general process parameter (GPP).

Neither PCMP-001 nor SOP-4001 sets a numerical threshold for "held well inside" or "narrow". PCR-007 therefore states, for each parameter, the size of its effect across its PAR and the margin of the PAR to the NOR, and it gives the reason for each class on these two values. A statistically significant effect does not by itself make a parameter critical. The classes are outcomes of the study and are reported in PCR-007.

# Proven acceptable ranges (planned analysis) {#sec-par}

A proven acceptable range is determined for each output with a criterion at this step and for each factor of the response-surface model. The outputs are pool aggregate, pool host cell protein and fragments. The criterion is the intermediate acceptance criterion of @tbl-iac, `{python} s_agg` % for aggregate, `{python} s_hcp` ng/mg for host cell protein and `{python} s_frag` % for fragments. At this step a PAR is the range of a parameter over which the eluate pool meets the level it must hand on to anion exchange.

Two analyses are run for every pair of factor and output, and both are reported.

1. The set-point analysis scans the factor across its range studied with the other factors at their set-points. At this step the set-points are also the centre of the design. The PAR is the contiguous range around the set-point over which the mean prediction, at manufacturing scale, meets the criterion. It shows what one parameter can do while the rest of the step is at target.
2. The NOR-propagated analysis scans the factor across `{python} s_grid` grid points of its range studied. At each grid point it draws `{python} s_mc` operating points for the other factors. Each factor is drawn from a normal distribution centred on its set-point, with a standard deviation of `{python} s_div` of the width of its NOR, and clipped to the range studied. This assumes that the NOR spans ±`{python} s_ksd` standard deviations of the routine variation of the parameter. Each draw also takes its own set of coefficients from the estimated sampling distribution of the fitted coefficients, and its own residual. The interval therefore includes the model residual and the uncertainty of the coefficients. The `{python} s_pi` prediction interval of a single batch runs from the `{python} s_pct_lo`th to the `{python} s_pct_hi`th percentile of the simulated batches. A grid point is acceptable when the `{python} s_pct_hi`th percentile, at manufacturing scale, does not exceed the criterion. The PAR is the contiguous range of acceptable grid points around the set-point.

The NOR-propagated PAR is the one that supports a claim. It is in general narrower than the set-point PAR, because the range must hold while the rest of the operating point moves around its set-point.

Where the acceptable settings are not contiguous, the contiguous part that contains the set-point is reported, and PCR-007 states that this has been done. Where the criterion is met across the whole range studied, the PAR is the range studied, and the claim stops at that range. A PAR that reaches the end of the range studied is reported as reaching it. Where an output does not meet its criterion even at the set-point, PCR-007 reports that no PAR exists for that output and states the consequence for the NOR. A parameter that affects several outputs has a PAR for each, and the range carried into the control strategy is their intersection (PCMP-001 §7.6). An output without an adequate model sets no range (@sec-adequacy).

Each output with an adequate model is shown in a plot of its predicted response against the parameter with the largest main effect on it. The plot shades the acceptable region green and marks the set-point and the NOR. The Monte Carlo analysis uses the fixed seed `{python} s_seed`, so a repeat of the analysis on the recorded data returns the same ranges.

A PAR is a statement about one parameter while the others are held at their set-points or drawn around them. The operating region of @sec-region is a statement about the `{python} k` factors together. A combination of settings that each lie inside their PAR may still fall outside the region where an interaction is active. Both are reported, and the control strategy is built on the region.

# Data management and integrity {#sec-data}

Data generated under this plan are recorded and kept under the ALCOA+ principles. Every result is attributable, legible, contemporaneous, original and accurate, and the record is complete, consistent, enduring and available. Run conditions and observations are recorded in the electronic laboratory notebook at the time of execution, with the date of each run, so that the execution window of each study is part of the record (@sec-schedule). The calibration status of each instrumented system on the dates of use is recorded with the study. Chromatograms and their integration are kept in the chromatography data system under audit trail. Analytical results are transferred from the validated instrument systems into the study data set without manual transcription wherever the systems allow, and a second person verifies any manual entry.

The analysis data set, the analysis scripts and the fitted models are kept with the report, so that every number in PCR-007 can be traced to the run that produced it. A recorded value may be changed after review only under the correction procedure, with the original value, the reason and the person who made the change retained.

A departure from an approved procedure or a good manufacturing practice (GMP) requirement, or an unplanned event during execution, is recorded as a deviation when it occurs. PCR-007 reports each deviation with its investigation, its root cause and its impact on the conclusions, whether or not a conclusion changes. Work that this plan does not foresee is not a deviation. PCR-007 records it as a discrepancy from the plan, with what the plan foresaw, what was done and why.

# Roles and responsibilities {#sec-roles}

Process Development and MSAT own this plan. They design the studies, run them on the scale-down model, analyse the data and write PCR-007. The other functions in @tbl-roles review and approve within their own competence, and no function approves its own work.

```{python}

T.frame(roles_tab, cap_roles, "tbl-roles", align=["P{4.8cm}", "P{10.6cm}"]).show()
```

A role may be held by more than one person, and one person may hold more than one role, provided that the person who reviews an analysis is not the person who made it. The names of the people in each role at execution are recorded in the study file and not in this plan, so that a change of staff does not need a revision of the plan.

# Deliverables and schedule {#sec-schedule}

The deliverable of this plan is PCR-007. It reports the execution of every study described here, the scale-down offsets and the qualification of the model for each output, and the fitted models with their adequacy. It also reports the operating region, the PARs, the capability estimate, the verification of the platform worst cases and the classification of each parameter. It carries the design matrices as executed, including any repeated run, every deviation recorded during the campaign and every discrepancy from this plan. PCR-007 rolls up into PCMR-001, which consolidates the characterization of the whole train.

The work runs in five phases.

1. The qualification runs are made and the offset of each output is estimated, before the first characterization run. Whether the model is qualified for each output is decided at analysis (@sec-qualification).
2. The screening study follows, and its analysis identifies the factors and interactions that change each response.
3. The response-surface study follows the screening analysis.
4. The univariate assessment of `{python} nm["flow"]` may run in parallel with either designed study, since it shares no material or equipment constraint with them.
5. The analysis, the qualification decision, the PAR determination, the capability estimate and the verification are made on the complete data set, and the report is written last.

@tbl-windows records the execution window of each study. A window opens on the day of the first laboratory run of the study and closes on the day of its last. Version 1.0 of this plan was approved on `{python} v1_date`, before the first window opened on `{python} first_start`. The qualification runs ended on `{python} S.loc["qualification", "end"]`, before the screening study began on `{python} S.loc["screening", "start"]`. The univariate assessment ran in parallel with the response-surface study, from `{python} S.loc["univariate", "start"]` to `{python} S.loc["univariate", "end"]`. The analytical method decision `{python} AMD["id"]` of `{python} AMD["date"]` fell within the response-surface study (@sec-methods).

# Risks and assumptions {#sec-risks}

Four risks to the study are recognized, and each has a response.

1. The scale-down model may differ from the commercial column in a respect the qualification does not test. Under the offset rule a difference in mean is acceptable when it is known precisely enough (@sec-qualification). The qualification does not compare the flow distribution inside the two columns, which plate count and peak asymmetry bound only indirectly. Should a difference in packing quality or flow distribution be found later, the affected conclusions would have to be revisited at scale.
2. The feed material may not be representative. The load is the neutralized pool of low-pH viral inactivation, and its aggregate and host cell protein content set the starting point of every clearance the study measures. Load attributes are measured on every run and reported with the results, so that a clearance can be told apart from a low starting level. Where a lot proves out of trend on any load attribute, the runs made on it should be identified in PCR-007 and their influence on the fitted models assessed.
3. The resin may behave differently at another point in its life cycle. All characterization runs are made on resin within the cycle count qualified under the resin life cycle procedure SOP-2008, and the conclusions are bounded by that cycle count. Performance at the end of the qualified life is established by the life cycle study, not here.
4. Assay variability may hide a small effect. The centre points give the reproducibility of each response under study conditions, and an effect smaller than that spread is not claimed.

Five assumptions are made.

1. The platform mechanisms apply to A-Mab at this step. The qualification and the centre point performance test this assumption, and the study does not take it as given.
2. The parameters of @tbl-params are the parameters that matter. RA-001 established this, and the study can test it only within its own factors.
3. A quadratic model describes the responses over the ranges studied. The tests of @sec-adequacy check this for each response.
4. The NOR of each parameter spans ±`{python} s_ksd` standard deviations of its routine variation. The NOR-propagated analysis rests on this assumption (@sec-par).
5. Fragments separate in the same way at both scales. The qualification does not compare them, so their judgement rests on the mechanism stated in @sec-sdm.
